quarantined_leads.lead: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to President Donald Trump and is expected to leave the post on or about September 3 after reported clashes with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
quarantined_leads.source_title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is stepping down after 18 months on the job, White House says
quarantined_leads.subject_response: The White House said Driscoll had been highly effective in advancing President Trump's agenda. The Army referred questions to the White House; no misconduct allegation or separate response from Driscoll was reported.
quarantined_leads.reason: The resignation and Trump-administration appointment are explicitly documented and were independently reported by the Associated Press and The Washington Post. The reports describe policy and management friction, anonymous-source claims about Pentagon dysfunction, and leadership turnover, but do not document an arrest, charge, ethics complaint, investigation, finding, discipline, retaliation adjudication, or other qualifying misconduct action involving Driscoll. Retained for follow-up without converting an ordinary resignation or reported internal disagreement into misconduct.
